title: Low gravity
purpose: Teach how one-sixth gravity changes walking, dust and braking on the Moon.

beats.label: diagram
beats.credit: Physics: the Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's

beats.label: diagram
beats.credit: Physics: no air on the Moon

captions: On the Moon you weigh about one-sixth of what you weigh on Earth.
So every step becomes a bound, and you float down slowly.
With no air, kicked-up dust flies in clean arcs and drops straight back.
Less weight on the wheels means less grip, so stopping takes longer.
ends_on: Move slower than feels natural, and leave yourself room to stop.
